site.name: Tomoshibi Atlas
site.tagline: Physical and mental health, and the challenges facing AI (SI), IT and social systems, on one globe.
purpose.title: About this site
purpose.body: This site places published information on infectious diseases, mental health and welfare, and medical research on the same globe as security threats to AI (SI), IT and social systems, and information on disasters and crime. By looking at people's health and the troubles of systems and society side by side, it aims to make their connections easier to notice and to help people prepare to live better.
purpose.relation: "Lights" are information about the systems that support people's health and daily lives. "Warnings" are information that needs attention: threats to the IT and AI that run those systems, and disasters and crime. For example, if a hospital's or a welfare office's systems are shut down by a cyberattack, the care and support themselves stop. "Research & Response" also includes results achieved with AI and official security, disaster and crime prevention measures. Where documents such as those of the US government call AI "SI" (Super Intelligence), the site treats them as AI information.
guide.title: Purpose & how to use
guide.howto.1: The globe rotates slowly. Drag to rotate; use the mouse wheel or two fingers to zoom.
guide.howto.2: Use the tabs at the top to switch topics. Tap a light or a headline to open the information for that area, with links to the original sources.
guide.howto.3: Search for a country or area, or press "My location", to move the globe there and stop.
guide.legend.1: Large headlines: items highlighted by fixed rules, such as recent publication (this is not a severity rating)
guide.legend.2: Faded "earlier report": a newer report exists for the same area and topic. Kept visible until 7 days after its own publication date
guide.legend.3: The dark side of the globe is where it is currently night; the faint orange band is around sunrise or sunset
caption.outbreak: Infectious diseases: WHO Disease Outbreak News, retrieved automatically twice a day. Each light marks a country named in the report.
caption.research: Research & Response: from peer-reviewed papers and announcements by public bodies, added after checking the original. Besides research in medicine and AI (SI), it includes official IT and AI security updates (such as patches) and official disaster and crime prevention measures.
caption.care: Mental health & Welfare: mental health statistics and support services, and the systems that support daily life with the challenges noted in official reports. Added after checking the original; statements about challenges reflect the cited source.
caption.security: IT security: announcements by public bodies, retrieved automatically twice a day. Each light marks the country of the publishing agency, not where an attack occurred or came from.
caption.crime: Crime prevention: warnings and statistics on scams, fraud and other crime from public bodies, added after checking the original, plus automatic headlines from public bodies abroad.
caption.disaster: Disasters: damage reports on typhoons, heavy rain, heat, fires and more published by public bodies. Not a source for emergencies.
caption.quake: Earthquakes: magnitude 5.5 or larger worldwide (preliminary public data from the U.S. Geological Survey, retrieved twice a day). Not a source for emergencies.

note.security: Only information already published by public bodies, such as vulnerabilities, is listed here. If you use an affected product or service, update it or follow the official guidance from the vendor or public authorities. To prevent misuse, this site does not publish how to carry out attacks or details that could be used in them.
notice.impersonation: This site never asks for personal information, passwords or money. If you are contacted by email, social media or phone by someone claiming to be this site or its operator, do not respond. You can also check whether a link is official by the domain shown (for example .gov).
add.title: Welfare guides, security steps and more
add.welfare: Welfare: the site also lists official places to ask for help in each country. Choose the Mental health & Welfare tab and select your country on the globe or by search; a list organised by type of problem appears at the bottom.
add.welfareBtn: Find your country in the Mental health & Welfare tab
add.security: IT security: besides threat information, the site will add steps that individuals using computers and smartphones can take, based on information from public bodies.
add.securityBtn: See security steps you can take
add.research: How mental health, infectious diseases and research connect: countries and international bodies are working on using AI and other tools to detect illness earlier, spot early signs of outbreaks and advance drug research (in Japan, for example, research developing AI to help detect depression earlier has been selected for public funding [FY2021 examples]). At the same time, there has been a case in Japan where a hospital's systems were stopped by a cyberattack and it suspended new outpatients. This site lets you switch between these research developments (Research & Response), the infectious diseases and mental health concerns actually occurring, and the security of the IT that supports them (IT security), while staying on the same region.
add.sources: Basis: WHO (2021 report on AI in health; 2021 Hub for Pandemic and Epidemic Intelligence), AMED (FY2021 programme on implementing AI in medicine), Japan's Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (2022 material on a cyberattack on a medical institution). Sources are listed on the About page.

meta.description: Tomoshibi Atlas (ともしびアトラス, "Atlas of Lights") is a non-profit site run by Yutaka Yoshioka (吉岡有隆). It shows public information on infectious diseases, mental health and welfare, and medical research alongside AI (SI) and IT security threats and disaster and crime information on one globe, with official links to support services in each country.
